q: What is a senior BA accountable for beyond writing requirements?
options: Connecting the need, decisions and delivery to measurable business value
why: Senior BAs lead analysis quality and connect it to outcomes without taking every decision.

q: A sponsor asks to replace a tool. What should the BA clarify first?
options: The underlying need and desired outcome
The color scheme of the replacement
Which vendor has the shortest name
why: Understanding the need prevents prematurely treating a proposed solution as the requirement.

q: Who normally owns the investment decision?
why: The BA informs the decision; the sponsor authorizes investment.

q: What best describes a senior BA individual contributor?
options: Leads through analysis, facilitation and judgment without necessarily managing staff
why: Senior scope can be an expert IC role and does not require line management.

q: Which chain best connects strategy to delivery?
options: Strategic objective → outcome → measure → change hypothesis → work
Project task → tool → team → strategy label
why: The chain preserves traceability from enterprise intent to concrete work.

q: Which outcome statement is most measurable?
options: Reduce high-risk breaks older than two days by 40% in six months
why: A strong outcome names a population, magnitude and time horizon.

q: Why should a BA clarify competing objectives?
options: Trade-offs must be made explicit when outcomes conflict
Stakeholders should all have identical priorities
It removes the need for a sponsor
It guarantees the project meets its date
why: Explicit priorities support informed decisions when goals such as speed and control compete.

q: Why use an operating model in analysis?
options: A system change may also affect roles, processes, information, controls and support
It is only a software deployment diagram
why: Operating models show the full set of elements required to deliver value.

q: What should the BA do with an apparent regional process exception?
options: Verify whether it comes from regulation, policy, system limits or habit
Assume it is required by law
Delete it from the target model
Treat it as a defect without discussion
why: Evidence helps distinguish necessary variation from inherited practice.

q: Which is an example of an operating-model dimension?
why: Operating models include roles and decision mechanisms along with process, data and technology.

q: What is a business capability?
options: A stable ability the organization needs, such as resolving exceptions
A list of individual employee tasks
why: Capabilities describe what the business must be able to do independent of current org charts.

q: What does a value stream show?
options: End-to-end stages through which a stakeholder receives value
why: Value streams connect work across handoffs from an initiating need to an outcome.

q: How should a capability map be used?
options: At the level needed to compare gaps and investment choices
As a decorative diagram with every task
As a replacement for all process maps
As proof that a solution will work
why: A map is useful when it informs decisions about capability gaps and change.

q: What should determine the depth of analysis?
options: Decision importance, uncertainty, risk and cost of being wrong
The number of meetings on the calendar
why: Analysis should be proportionate to the decision and its consequences.

q: What is a useful hypothesis in early discovery?
options: A testable explanation for the observed problem
A confirmed fact that cannot change
why: A hypothesis focuses discovery and should be tested against evidence.

q: What should accompany an unresolved assumption?
options: Its impact, confidence, owner and a way to test it
A final approval date regardless of evidence
why: Assumptions need ownership and validation based on their consequence if false.

q: What is the purpose of a roadmap?
options: Sequence outcomes, dependencies and decision points over time
Promise every delivery task as fixed
why: A roadmap gives leaders a view of outcome sequencing and important dependencies.

q: Why might a data-quality foundation appear before a visible product feature?
options: It enables later automation and reduces risk
It is always the cheapest work
why: Enabling work may be required before downstream value can be safely achieved.

q: How should roadmap items be reviewed?
options: When evidence, dependencies or business priorities change
why: Roadmaps should adapt to material changes while keeping decisions deliberate.

q: What distinguishes a senior BA recommendation from a preference?
options: It states supporting evidence, trade-offs, conditions and what could change the view
why: A defensible recommendation explains rationale and uncertainty.

q: When is a pilot especially useful?
options: When it can reduce important uncertainty before a costly scale-up
When all evidence is already conclusive
When no owner can be assigned
When the team wants to avoid measuring outcomes
why: Pilots are valuable when they produce evidence that changes a larger decision.
